stem: A child has unilateral eyelid erythema and swelling. Which additional finding most strongly suggests orbital cellulitis rather than preseptal cellulitis?

options.A: Pain with eye movement and proptosis
options.B: Normal visual acuity and full painless extraocular movements
options.D: Eyelid swelling with preserved ocular motility

rationale: Current AAO EyeWiki guidance identifies proptosis, pain with eye movements, and impaired extraocular motility as findings suggestive of orbital involvement. Preseptal cellulitis is generally confined anterior to the orbital septum and is characterized by eyelid erythema/edema with preserved visual acuity and ocular movements. Therefore A is the best discriminator in this vignette.
educational_objective: Differentiate orbital cellulitis from preseptal cellulitis by recognizing pain with eye movement and proptosis as signs of deeper orbital involvement.
source_version_date: Orbital Cellulitis page reviewed Up to Date 2026-02-07; current pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Orbital Cellulitis > Diagnosis: signs suggestive of orbital involvement include proptosis, pain with eye movements and ophthalmoplegia; Preseptal Cellulitis > Diagnosis: preseptal cellulitis has normal visual acuity, absence of proptosis, and normal ocular movements, whereas orbital cellulitis has proptosis and reduced extraocular movements with pain
source_claim_supported: Pain with eye movement, proptosis, and impaired ocular motility favor orbital cellulitis over preseptal cellulitis.

correction_summary: Reframed the item from a broad statement about why orbital cellulitis is 'more concerning' to a clinically specific differentiation task. Limited the key to directly supported orbital signs and removed unnecessary urgency/treatment claims.
audit_findings: A directly matches current AAO EyeWiki differentiating features. B, C, and D describe preserved ocular function or superficial eyelid findings that are more compatible with preseptal disease and do not show the deeper orbital signs in A. Eyelid edema and erythema alone occur in both conditions, so the final stem intentionally asks for an additional discriminator. No second answer, treatment assumption, or unsupported numeric precision remains. NCSBN 2026 supports the Physiological Adaptation mapping through Pathophysiology and Illness Management.
